column3: “Had come into days” is rendered “advanced in age.”
“Stand before the king” is rendered “attend the king.”
“Did not know her” is rendered “did not cohabit with her.”
“Had not rebuked him from his days” is rendered “had never crossed him at any time.”
“His words were with” is rendered “he had conferred with.”
“Come and go” is rendered “Go at once.”
“What is to you?” is rendered “What do you wish?”
Close to the Hebrew; many manuscripts read “and you” for the second “and now.”
NASB supplies “now”; some manuscripts read “and now” for “and you.”
“Sinners” is rendered “will be considered offenders,” and NASB adds “Otherwise.”
“May the king live” is rendered “Long live King Adonijah!”
The Hebrew “your servant” (written text) is rendered “your servants.”
“Swore an oath” is rendered “vowed,” and “ransomed” as “redeemed.”
